title: Gwinnett couple warn others after losing $800K in cryptocurrency scam

reading.body:
A cryptocurrency scam used an AI-generated website to display false account balances to a victim, creating the appearance of legitimate investment returns. The fake website ran on top of a real trading app, showing fabricated account information that convinced the victim his money was growing. This is a system deployed without verification, where no human checked whether the account statements the victim saw matched reality before funds were transferred.

The scammer established trust through incremental withdrawals that succeeded, then requested larger amounts the victim could not access. The failure occurred at the point where the victim relied entirely on what appeared on his screen rather than on confirmation from the trading platform itself or a third party. It would have taken direct verification with the platform through a separate channel to catch the deception before the full loss occurred.

It is not established how the scammers gained access to the victim's account, how long the fake website remained functional, or what technical measures the legitimate trading app had in place to prevent such impersonation.

reports.title: Georgia couple loses $800K in sophisticated cryptocurrency scam
Gwinnett couple warn others after losing $800K in cryptocurrency scam

summary:
A retired Georgia couple lost nearly their entire life savings of $800,000 in a sophisticated cryptocurrency scam that started with a WhatsApp message. Jerry and Mindy Dunaway were contacted by a stranger who convinced Jerry to invest through a mobile trading app. The scammer gradually increased the investment amounts and allowed Jerry to withdraw small sums to build trust and confidence in the scheme. When Jerry attempted a larger withdrawal last week, he discovered the funds were inaccessible and contacted police.

Investigators determined that while the trading app was legitimate, scammers had created a fake AI-generated website that displayed false account information on Jerry's screen. The couple reported losing approximately $800,000 and is now working with Gwinnett County police, though authorities warn that victims in similar cases rarely recover their money. The Dunaways are publicly warning others about the sophisticated tactics used by scammers, and their children have started a GoFundMe campaign to help their parents with daily expenses.
